pagedata.pyLabel: open and lock the work object
pagedata.pyUsage: Called whenever an assignment is processed. Usually calling activity just aborts if SuccessIndicator parameter is less than zero, but ProcessAssignment and the function ServiceLevelEvent handle each case. This activity sets the following values in the parameter SuccessIndicator (-1 to -20 inherited from WorkLock): 0 - no errors -1 - work object not found -2 - work object open access denied -3 - work object's lock held by another -4 - work object modify access denied (lock fail) -5 - cover object not found -6 - cover object open access denied -7 - cover object's lock held by another -8 - cover object modify access denied (lock fail) -9 - lockstring fail -10 - miscellaneous database failure -21 - corresponding flow on work object is at different task -22 - corresponding flow on work object no longer exists -23 - work object points to different assignment -24 - Rule-Obj-Flow no longer exists -25 - Rule-Obj-Flow exists, but the assignment shape has been deleted -26 - assignment's pxFlowName property is blank -27 - Perform Assignments security fail Parameter FailureInfo contains the error message Parameter FailureMsgDesc contains the fieldvalue key for localizing the message (only some have this) For locking errors -3, -7, and -9 the clipboard page LockInfo contains further information.

rowdata.pxWarningMessage: Writing application logic using the Java activity method impacts maintainability, discourages reusability, and increases risk during upgrades. Use this method only when necessary. If executing Java code is required, consider using the Call-Function activity method to execute a Function rule. Using Function rules encourages creating well-defined input and output parameters and can be reused across many different types of rules.
The use of activity rules should be limited. The need for activities can be reduced by using data transforms, as well as techniques such as case management, the Engine API, and declaratives.
